minutes.headline: Finance Committee discussed FY25 level-service school budget, override ideas, and facilities consolidation; approved prior minutes.
minutes.summary: The committee discussed how to review FY25 department budgets line by line and post them publicly, health insurance news, and possible consolidation of town and school facilities. The chair shared the superintendent's level-service school budget and a possible override range. The committee also took up a grant writer letter, heard two residents, approved two sets of minutes and adjourned.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, parent, CPA, member of the Musicator committee
public_comment.topic: Supported hiring a grant writer, said professional grant writers exist and should pay for themselves, and said an override should be considered.
Suggested a grant-writing committee in town and putting money under contractual services, so a grant writer is supported by organization and leadership.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of January 18th and January 25th.

budget_items.what_was_said: The final health insurance increase was reported as under the state average, expected to help both town and school budgets.
The snow and ice line is deliberately budgeted low and routinely overspent, with the actual spend running far higher.
The superintendent's level-service budget was far above the town manager's requested increase for the schools.
A member questioned the health insurance, electricity, building maintenance and collaborative tuition increases, and asked whether circuit breaker offsets are included.
Members asked why the high school guidance line and a new elementary social worker line rose; one suggested ESSER-funded positions are being absorbed.
The school faces an additional expense for reverse 911 compliance.
A member asked how circuit breaker funding for special education is built into the budget; the special ed director will present on it Feb 28.
A member said a part-time non-benefited grant writer would be a tiny share of the budget.
The grant cap per round is described as dropping after cumulative awards approach a limit.
The assessors voted to recommend adding to the overlay account despite a sizable existing balance, funded earlier from free cash.
The Board of Health budget is up from last year, driven by fees paid for nurses and health services.

decisions.decision: Chair will ask the IT person and town manager about posting department line-item budgets on the Finance Committee web page.
A joint conversation on facilities consolidation will be put on the agenda for May or June, after budget season.
A draft grant writer letter is to be prepared for the next weekly meeting, with the clerk to finalize and send it.
Calendar noted: public hearing March 28, committee report due April 2, town meeting May 4, election May 18.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no recorded votes on a school budget or override; it heard the superintendent's FY25 level-service school budget and discussed a possible override range.
Members questioned school line increases, including health insurance, electricity, building maintenance, collaborative tuition and guidance and social worker lines.
The committee agreed to put a joint conversation on town and school facilities consolidation on the agenda for May or June, after budget season.
A draft grant writer letter is to be prepared for the next weekly meeting, with the clerk to finalize and send it.
The committee approved two sets of prior minutes and adjourned after noting the March hearing, April report and May town meeting dates.

why_it_matters: The school's level-service request, set beside the town manager's requested increase for the schools, is the gap that an override discussion would try to close, and an override is a vote residents would be asked to take.

Whether school lines rise because costs grew or because expired grant money (such as ESSER) is landing on the town budget is not settled in the minutes, and the answer changes what the town is asked to pay.
